title: Bishkek Sunday marches for legality / against the “Khanstitution”
location: Central Bishkek, including the railway station to Ala-Too Square / Erkindik Boulevard
participants_original: Jan 10 source search result: police about 30; organizers 50. Jan 31 Kloop search result: organizers said more than 20. Neither count is transferable across Sundays.
notes: The weekly march series began before this unit. ACLED/Oxus reports mid-October 2020 through adoption of amendments on Jan 10; IPHR/CIVICUS says such Sunday marches were regularly held since November 2020; Azattyq search result calls Jan 10 the tenth march; Kloop’s Jan 31 search-result archive reports a further march. These accounts create uncertainty whether weekly assemblies are one continuing episode or distinct actions and contradict the apparent Jan 10 end. No attendee count from one date is applied to another. The separately opened ACLED HTML page repeats the same report as S005 and is not an independent source. Newly read Kloop Jan 17 report identifies an eleventh weekly march, confirming activity after Jan 10; Kloop archive lists Jan 3 as the ninth, while Jan 3 body remains search-only. Search-only Jan 10 sources report about 30 by police and about 50 by organizers; Kaktus also reports about 50 but numbers the march differently. These are distinct-date leads, not a transferable campaign headcount. Kloop’s Jan 31 search-result text confirms another Sunday march against constitutional change and an organizer estimate of more than 20, while providing no upper bound. Separate date record E008 remains a search-only discovery lead. A March 1 Media.kg search result quotes organizer Ulan Usein saying four months of weekly marches and 16 actions had occurred by then; it supports later continuation but is retrospective and no individual January count is inferred.

start_date.summary: ACLED/Oxus says mid-October; IPHR/CIVICUS retrospectively describes Sunday marches since November, so exact start is not resolved.

continuity.summary: ACLED/Oxus says until Jan 10; contemporaneous Jan10 and Jan31 search results, plus later IPHR/CIVICUS account of a series, indicate marches on both dates and regular Sunday activity.

location.summary: Retrieved reports describe central Bishkek routes from the railway station to Ala-Too Square / White House.

participants_original.summary: Separate search-result attendance descriptions for Jan10 and Jan31; do not conflate or carry across the weekly series. Additional separate Jan 3 (~50) and Jan 10 (police ~30 / organizers ~50) search-only counts and Jan 17 no-count report are not transferable across dates. Jan 31 search result says more than 20 with no upper bound.

open_questions: Resolve the exact first march and whether October or November is the appropriate start; only month-level start is retained.
Determine whether the manual’s event unit treats each weekly physical march as a separate action or a continuing episode; the additional Coding Procedure is missing.
Determine continuation after Jan 31 and physical end, not inferred from referendum date or later article publication.
If Jan 10 is coded as a discrete meeting, verify count from a readable body; search-only estimate was 30 police / 50 organizers.
What occurred on Jan 3, Jan 10, Jan 17, Jan 24 and Jan 31 as separate physical actions, and which source bodies can be read?
Resolve discrepancy in Jan 10 march number (Azattyq: tenth; Kaktus: ninth) without assuming same source count or day.
